children: The EU-standard harmonised inflation rate (HICP) in Ireland quickened to 3.4% year-on-year in August 2026 from a five-month low of 3.1% in July, according to preliminary estimates.
The main upward pressure came from energy prices, which surged by 11.8%, after a 6.5% advance in the previous month.
Meanwhile, services inflation remained steady at 3.7%, while food price growth slowed significantly to 0.1% from 0.8%.
Excluding energy and unprocessed food, harmonised inflation moderated to 2.6%, down from 2.9% in the previous month.
On a monthly basis, harmonised consumer prices rose by 0.6% in August, the most in five months, up from a 0.1% in the month before, propelled by energy costs (+4.3%).

title: Ireland Harmonised Inflation Rate Inches Higher to 3.4%
